Re: The OFFICIAL cannabis growing thread
You should be able to grow some good outdoors weed in your climate. Weed is an annual plant which germinates, flowers and produces seed all in one year. It likes fairly a growing medium of fairly neutral PH. If you have gardening experience then you should know about seed germination, using wet paper towels to germinate seeds has a high success rate, just be careful with the seeds once the taproot has developed. The seeds should take 2-10 days to germinate, some are quicker and some are slower. Keep the towels moist, not soaking wet.

There should be no fertilisation of cannabis plants while in germination/seedling stage. Once the seed has developed a tap root you can transplant it into some compost to develop into a seedling. Your seedling can grow quite well under fluorescent light or in indirect sunlight and you should keep it under this light until it has developed at least 3 pairs of branches. When it's established itself as a plant you can begin to harden it off to the outside climate, putting it in a sheltered spot for a few hours every day, gradually increasing the amount of time it's spending outside. If the leaves start to turn a pale green it's time to feed your plants with a balanced NPK fertiliser diluted to a quarter of the recommended amount on the packet/bottle. When the plant has been hardened off to the outside climate you'll want to prepare a hole to plant it in(I'm guessing you're planting in the ground and not keeping it in a pot outside). Dig a 1ft x 1ft square hole and fill with a mixture of sand, compost a small handful of dolomite lime and a small handful of fish, blood and bone. Mix all of this up in the hole and transplant your plant into the hole. If you plant your plant outside in Mid May you should be able to have some killer weed by mid september. If you're buying seeds over the internet then consider femaleseeds.nl and their Easy Sativa strain.

If the weather is especially hot and dry you might need to water the plant every day when its outside, if the leaves wilt in the heat then you'll need to give your plant lots of water. Check for fungus and mould regularly if the weather is humid. Growing outside is fairly simple and just takes common sense more than anything else.

Re: The OFFICIAL cannabis growing thread
I'll assume your talking about seeds?

The main difference is that darker seeds have matured in the calyx on the marijuana plant and the lighter seeds are immature and not as suitable for germination as darker seeds because they are immature. Seed colours and patterns change depending on the genetics of a plant also, some strain's seeds will look relatively pale when mature compared to another strain which could have a dark marbled coating or be dark all over. This may sound strange but good seeds look pretty.

If you're talking about darker colour plants; many cannabis plants take on a red/purple hue when subjected to a cold environment. Some strains display different coloured hues due to their genetics, there is a European variety which is completely black and unless the genetic pool is interfered with the strain will always breed black plants.

Re: The OFFICIAL cannabis growing thread
As much as the type of smoker you describe yourself as disgusts me I'll endeavour to answer your questions.

Taking "most" to mean approximately 10, you'll probably get 5 females out of them and of those five two may survive. For two plants packed very closely together 43W of fluoro will not be ample for a respectable harvest. You really should let them mature to at least 3 weeks before putting them into 12/12. They are only in the seedling stage now and will take 1 1/2 weeks to 2 weeks to get into vegetative.

If you could get four or five 20w energy saver bulbs and fit them above the plants also your grow space would benefit immensely. You should be able to get cheap energy saver bulbs for 99c or so each and the fittings don't cost much more. The 150w or so of light would be a lot more suitable for a couple of plants.

Cannabis plants producing most of their THC in the first four weeks is not quite true. Different plants vary and most plants develop more THC in the last four weeks of flowering. To harvest your plants after flowering them for only four weeks is not advised, it is much more sensible to watch the plant develop for a month or two waiting for pre-flowers. Once the plant shows its pre-flowers it is telling you what sex it is, now you can kill the males and keep the pretty females for flowering.

You want a small SOG right? Well the way SOG's are usually done is with clones from Bushy mature plants, because the clones are easy to keep uniform and are the same age as the mature mother plant so they can flower immediately.

Flowering starts as soon as you switch the lights to 12/12 really, plants immediately react to the change in light cycle. Although it can take 7-10 days for visibly noticeable changes in the plant.

THC content degrades when exposed to light and fluorescent lights are quite cool so they won't dry weed very well. It'd be best to just set the buds on the newspaper and cover with more newspaper, turning the buds twice a day and keeping them in a fairly well ventilated and dry room.

This (http://www.uk420.com/boards/index.php?showtopic=38959) is a pretty good guide to harvesting and curing.

Squeegee, regenerational growing is somewhat viable for getting two harvests out of one plant but the second harvest will always be fairly minimal compared to the first and the time involved in reverting a plant to vegetative to build up sugars and then putting back into flowering could be put to much better use tending to a mother plant and taking clones. Cloning is more popular than regenerational groing for a good reason, it's more dependable and you get better results for the effort put in.

The most you can really get out of a plant is two harvests with regenerational growing because the plant is an annual it just isn't made to be regenerated and flower again.

It's best to keep one or two plants in 24/0 as mothers and make clones for a hydro system.

This way you could have a perpetual harvest system rather than waiting to regenerate a plant for small amounts of bud.

Hydroponic nutrients could quite likely be found at your local nursery but your best bet would be with canna hydroponics nutrients from a headshop or bought online. A good hydro set up could use canna coco coir and canna A + B Nutrients, I don't mean to advertise them but they'll give damn good results.

I've seen varying reports about Nottingham Seedbank, it's pretty much always best to buy direct from the seedbank if you can or official seedshops for the seedbank.

Here's some good seedsites which are reliable and have top quality well priced seeds:

http://www.greenhouseseeds.nl/enter.html Go to the Available section and scroll down to the bottom, you should find they're selling 5 Himalayan Gold seeds for 19.00.

www.sensiseeds.com (http://www.sensiseeds.com) Under Whitelabel you should be able to find their White Skunk seeds, 12.00 for 16 seeds. Have a few of them on the go miself.

Am growing Grapefruit, Northern Lights, Grapefruit x Northern Lights and C99 from them and all the plants are incredibly vigorous. The handy thing is you can buy packs of 4/5 for around 20 and get a really good mother plant out of those seeds.

http://www.hemcy.com/open.html Hemcy has some real nice strains and although they're all over 40 for 12 you could do worse than get some of their Inca Spirit 80/£55.

Also, check out http://www.bcbudonline.com for some nice strains too, they're a bit costly but quality is high.

For lots of good cheap seeds sensiseeds is very good, their WhiteSkunk, Skunk#1 and Sensi Skunk are all very good cheap seeds.

Re: The OFFICIAL cannabis growing thread
Tissue culture is basically the practice of cutting a little bit of a leaf off and placing it in a special solution which encourages the plant cells to multiply to the point of creating a whole new plant with roots, leaves and stem from a small piece of a plant's leaf.

More in depth:

Items Needed for Home Tissue Culture:

1 - A sterile still air cabinet used to transfer plants. A fish tank on its side makes an ideal transfer cabinet. Any perspex or glass chamber with dimensions of 50 cm (length), 40 cm (height) and 40 cm (depth) could easily be made into a transfer cabinet.

2 - A pressure cooker for sterilisation of media, instruments, water, paper towelling etc.

3 - Glass jars (baby food jars are excellent) and take away food containers with lids which can withstand the heat inside a pressure cooker are ideal vessels to use.

4 - Scalpel and forceps

5 - Paper towelling or even A4 white copy paper, cut to size, can be sterilised and used for a sterile cutting surface.

6 - A spirit lamp containing ethanol for flaming the instruments (avoid using Methanol as it is toxic!).

7 - Hand held spray bottle containing 70% alcohol solution to spray the transfer chamber and other surfaces.

8 - Dilute chlorine solution e.g. 1/4 dilution of the household bleach (e.g. White King) for use in surface sterilisation of plant material.

9 - Any skin disinfectant e.g. Hibitane (obtainable from any chemist shop).

10 - Media (see below)

Media Preparation

All the ingredients indicated below can be purchased using the super market, chemist and a health food shop.

1- Two cups of rain water

2- A quarter cup of sugar

3- Fertiliser stock: 1/2 tablespoon all purpose 10:10:10 (N.P.K.) water soluble fertiliser in 1L of water: use one cup of stock for this recipe.

4- Inositol tablets (500 mg): 1/2 tablet

5- Vitamin tablet with thiamine: 1/2 tablet- Any multivitamin tablet may be used.

6- Agar flakes: 4 tablespoons

This is the basic media. For preparation of multiplication and rooting media add 1/2 cup of coconut milk and 1/2 teaspoon of malt. Replacing the coconut milk with 1/2 cup of green tomato puree or 1/2 cup of freshly squeezed orange juice may produce different responses. Ensure that the pH of medium is always between 5 and 6 using narrow range pH indicator tape. Adjust pH if necessary, with acid e.g. Citric acid or base e.g bicarb soda.

Mix the ingredients in a saucepan and gently boil until the agar has dissolved, stirring continuously to stop the agar sticking and subsequently burning at the bottom of the pan. Dispense into empty glass jars, using a ladle, so that the medium is about 2 cm deep. Cover and process in a pressure cooker. Cook for 15 minutes after the pressure is reached (this will be achieved when the pressure valve starts letting steam out).

Sterilising Instruments and Other Items

Forceps and scalpels can be sterilised by being wrapped in Alfoil and cooked in the pressure cooker for 15 minutes. These items can also be sterilised by being washed in chlorine solution or being dipped in alcohol and flamed.

Sterile water is needed for rinsing plant material and sterile paper towelling to be used as a clean surface to work on. The manipulation can be accomplished on the paper. When the operation is completed, the towel can be discarded and a new sterile surface selected from the sterile supply. The water can be sterilised in glass jars. Place paper inside a paper bag and cook them in the pressure cooker above the water level. The bag will be wet on completion of sterilisation. Transfer the bag to an oven set at 80 C and allow the bag to dry inside the oven. Do not unwrap the papers until needed.

Sterilisation of Plant Material

All plant material can be sterilised in diluted domestic bleach, for example White King (1/4 cup of White King + 3/4 cup of water + 1 drop of detergent- detergent acts as surfactant). Put plant pieces in a jar containing the bleach for 10-20 minutes. Agitate frequently. Discard the chlorine solution, this process will kill bacteria and fungi and sometimes some parts of the plant such as outer bud scales and softer shoots. Rinse plant pieces twice with sterile water.

Operations in the Sterile Cabinet

Great care should be taken to ensure that your cultures are free from contamination. To achieve this do the followings:

1- Tie back your hair, roll your sleeves up and remove your watch and other jewellery. Wash your hands thoroughly with the disinfectant solution suitable for skin application. If allergic to any disinfectant wash your hands with water and wear a pair of surgical gloves.

2- Sterilise the inside of the cabinet by spraying with 70% alcohol and wiping dry with sterile tissue.

3- Collect and organise all the items you will need close to or inside the cabinet.

4- Working in the cabinet, take a sterilised piece of stem from the jar with a pair of forceps (do not touch the plant material with your hands). Also sterilise your instruments by dipping them in alcohol between each manipulation and flaming them. Small pieces, 2-3 cm long with a few leaves can be cut and transferred to agar medium. If the leaves are too large either remove them or cut them to 1/3-1/2 the size. Put one piece of the shoot into each container (it is important to have only one shoot per container at this stage so that if the shoot is contaminated it cannot spread to the others). Shut the lids of the containers. Store jars at room temperature away from direct sunlight. Leave these shoots for one month.

One of these three things will happen during this time: some of the shoots will be killed by the chlorine solution and or the toxin produced by plants themselves; some will be contaminated by fungi and bacteria; or new shoots will grow very rapidly from the axils of the stems in the uncontaminated containers. Discard the dead and infested cultures.

Shoot Multiplication

The shoots from the previous stage may have elongated during the past four weeks. They need to be transferred to the medium containing the coconut milk (coconut milk has some growth promotory properties which makes plant segments to produce more shoots) for further multiplication.

1- Repeat the preparation and sterilisation steps for the medium, instruments and chamber as before. Sterilise your hands as before too.

2- Transfer the containers of shoots to one side of the cabinet and the sterilised medium at the other side.

3- Use sterile paper towelling, scalpels and forceps as before.

4- With a pair of forceps, remove a stem from its container, and cut on the surface of the sterile paper towelling moistened with some sterile water. It is important to do all the manipulation on a damp paper towel as these plants are very soft and can desiccate readily. The separated shoots can be transferred to the new jars. At this stage, up to five pieces of plant may be put inside each container.

5- Store cultures as explained in the previous stage.

The multiplication stage may be repeated every four weeks until enough plants have been obtained. As a general rule shoots can multiply 3-4 folds every four weeks. The important point to note here is that high rate of contamination during this stage suggests that you are getting air borne contaminants due to poor hygiene.

Root Formation

Once you have established enough shoots, let them grow to at least 2 cm before beginning the rooting process. Transfer shoots to the rooting medium containing coconut milk and malt. Up to five shoots may be put in each culture vessel. Store containers in their usual place as before. Roots should form within two to four weeks.

Transfer to Potting Mix (Acclimatisation)

The operation at this stage is carried out on the open bench. The rooted cultures can be treated as follows:

1- Fill the pots with suitable potting mix without any fertiliser and water well. Allow to drain.

2- Remove the rooted plants from agar medium using a pair of forceps.

3- Wash off the agar thoroughly from the roots using lukewarm water.

4- Insert a hole in the middle of the potting mix and gently insert the roots in that hole.

5- Spray the foliage with a hand spray containing water. These pots can be kept inside a larger plastic containers with a glass cover, out of the direct sunlight. Gradually remove the glass cover but watch for signs of desiccation and if needed use the hand spray to spray water on the foliage.

6- When the roots are well established and the plants are acclimatised (this should take about 4-6 weeks), they can be given fertiliser and be treated like any other plant. It is advisable to gradually increase the light intensity for the plants too.

The International Association for Plant Tissue Culture (http://tinyurl.com/yko838).

colorsoc, your best bet would be either the tarp idea or clear polyethylene held up with some lengths of wood, it won't keep your plants hidden too well but it'd work at keeping the rain out.

trippydeath, nice seeds (http://www.hempcity.net/travelreports/spain2004/cannabisgarden2004/image014.jpg) should be fairly dark. Some have marbled surfaces of dark and light and some are quite dark all over but white seeds are immature and will most likely not germinate at all.

Putting the seed in some soil out in the forest to germinate would cut your chances of it growing to even less. It's always best to germinate inside in a somewhat controlled environment and transplant the seedling once it has established itself somewhat.

None, growing is a good life experience and if you can get seeds for free then it could be fun. If you have about $500 or so to put into growing then you could have a good little grow which could change your outlook on many things.

Shadow Operative, there are a lot of websites for ordering seeds. The most reliable are the sites operated by the actual seed companies i.e.

http://www.nirvana-shop.com

http://www.femaleseeds.nl

http://www.sensiseeds.com

http://www.hemcy.com

http://www.dutch-passion.nl

http://www.seriousseeds.com

http://www.highestseeds.com

http://www.somaseeds.nl

http://www.dnagenetics-amsterdam.com

http://www.magusgenetics.com

http://www.thseeds.com

There are of course many more sites but there's a few. Most take Credit Card or Postal Order, some take cash, western union transfers etc.

jimbobjones, the sites above will serve you high quality seeds. For a first timer who wants high quality weed it could be worth your while to check out Grapefruit x NL from Femaleseeds. It is a very good cross and grows vigorously, the end product(if grown ok) will be the envy of pretty much any smoker you know. I've been smoking some SAGE recently which would be an ambitious grow for a first timer but I must say if you want good fucking weed try some SAGE. It is STRONG weed and a delight to be high on.

If you buy from seedbanks your purchase will be more reliable than if you buy from a person growing hobby weed for themselves or bagseeds because you will be dealing directly with the company who breed the seeds you buy. They put a fuck load of work into breeding the seeds to bring to you as good a quality as they can and the strains(unless otherwise stated) should be quite stable and not differ too much from one plant to the next. Whereas with bagseed or a friend's seeds from their pollinated crop will not be stable, you'll get interesting and sometimes nice plants but it's not a great place to start off from it's kinda like learning to swim with a blindfold on.

BazookaMedic, the qualities of excellent bud are variable dependant on personal preference. Some people like high trippy weed, some people like pain killing lethargic weed, some people like a mix of both etc.

Excellent bud will have to have been flushed of nutrients for a couple of weeks before harvest so the bud tastes of bud and not any residual nutrients not used up by the plant. It'll have to have been dried properly in an airy atmosphere with relative humidity around 50% and dried for a month at least. after drying it should be cured for another month at least in an airtight container in a cool, dark, dry place being checked and moved around inside the jar every few days. But really this is just what should be done with bud not the qualities of excellent bud. I'm not sure what the qualities of excellent bud are but when you find them you sure know you've found them. * and * have spent over ten thousand euros in the past couple of months in an attempt to produce a good environment to grow excellent bud, * had many discussions about what qualities to look for in the high of different buds but know that from one plant to the next the differences can be extreme and both plants can have excellent bud with completely different qualities.

I have a question regarding cold temperatures.

When it gets cold outside, is it the temperature that kills plants or is it the frost?

I'm thinking of building a small grow room, enough for one or two plants, in my attic. My attic has no heat, but there is almost no humidity. I live in SC, so the temp probably won't get under 15-20 throughout the winter. Would they grow slow or just die?
 #98 
2006-11-16, 17:56
[{{ªÞE×}}]
Regular
  
Re: The OFFICIAL cannabis growing thread
It's the temperature that'll kill the plants. 15-20 would be -6 to -9 Celsius which could easily kill the plants if they're exposed to the temperature for an extended period of time. Your best bet would be to pick up some glass fibre insulation from a hardware store and make sure the attic is well insulated. If you can switch the light cycle to 12 hours light at night and 12 hours dark during the day it'll help keep the plants warm during the coldest temperatures.

From Ask Ed: quote:

Temperatures below 50 degrees slow growth in most varieties of marijuana. When the temperature drops below 40 degrees, the plants may experience some damage and require about 24 hours to resume growth. Low nighttime temperatures may delay or prevent bud maturation. Some equatorial varieties stop growth after a few 40 degree nights.

You want to keep temperature differences between night and day inside of 10 degrees or the plants will be stressed. Below 45 plant cells begin to suffer and you'll notice the plants wilting etc.

even if the above conditions are met you will not be able to flower during the winter. This is because after dec 21 the light hours begin to steadily increase and wont begin to drop until june 21st. Of course this doesnt apply if your south of the equator where the opposite applies.

CarbonB

Re: The OFFICIAL cannabis growing thread
To get a pound off one plant on an indoor grow would take a very skilled grower and a very large plant.

Typically what people shoot for is 1g of weed per 1w of light. So if you have 400W of lighting, you are a pretty damn good grower if you can get 400g a grow with it. This isn't most growers though, and usually you get about .5g per watt when you are starting out, even lower.

That is still good though, 7 oz. of quality weed with 1 400W light is damn impressive. When I started out I think I got maybe 2 oz. off of 2 plants. Now I get around 3 oz. per plant and I can fit 2 - 3 plants in my particular area. That is upwards of 9 oz. if everything is optimal.

Depending on the size of the plant before it goes into flower, the strain and how well it yields, plus the light, plus ever other enviormental issue that could go wrong will effect how much you get at the end of harvest. You just have to grow, practice, perfect, and execute.

Doing all this will assure you plenty of quality bud all the time to smoke. Imagine, how long would it take you to go through 9 oz. of hydroponic sensimilia? Would take me a long time. Considering I might only smoke 4 or 5 grams in a week.

Each box is 96qt, meaning over a cubic foot of area per plant and a huge reservoir for the pump. The boxes will get spray painted black to keep the mold down, and will be covered with a thick rubber shop mat to keep the Perlite in place and prevent mold growth. The plants will be started with jiffy pots. I am thinking it should flood 12 times a day, depending on how fast the water runs out.

Without a timer, lights, grow nutrients, or a light reflector, the cost breakdown looks like this:

3, 33x16x13.6 containers - $30

36x48 heavy duty shop rug, $15

24, 8qt bags of Perlite, $72

130-170 gph fountain pump, $22

2 cans spray paint, ~$5

Electrical tap, piping for the splitter - ~$5

Basically $150 before taxes. I am thinking a 400watt HPS / MH light would be good for it, since it is less than 3x3 feet.

Lastly there should be a few grown in good old dirt with good old potting soil, as a fall-back.

2007-01-09, 05:35
tibberous
Regular
  
Re: The OFFICIAL cannabis growing thread
I'm not an expert, but since it is currently in a soup can, I'll give my advice.

I think your biggest problem will be the lip of the can, and since the plants roots are only going to get bigger, I'd recommend transplanting it asap. Find a pot the size you plan on it getting, and mix up some good soil. I can't comment first hand, but a video on youtube recommended something like %60 potting soil, %15 perlite, %10 worm casings, %10 masons sand and %5 premix. In fact, if your on cable, the youtube video's will give you a pretty good idea all around.

Use another soup can to make sure your new hole is the perfect size. Let the plant dry out enough that it doesn't want to clump in the can but not so dry it crumbles. Then just turn it upside down, pat it out, and dump it in your new hole. Only other way to do it would be to get the soil pretty well saturated then cut the can apart with tin snips or a dremmel, but if your going to go that route I'd just use tin snips and watch my fingers, since anything that doesn't pull the steel away from the can when cutting will end up cutting some distance into the dirt and possibly the roots.

Re: The OFFICIAL cannabis growing thread
quote:Originally posted by shadow operative:

As for the white widow is there any chance of it surviving being grown outdoors?

..It's fucking weed dude, it'll grow pretty damn much anywhere.. the question you should be asking is how the quality will be if grown outdoors. Widow will certainly do better in controlled conditions, but I've known a few people who have grown it outdoors with success. Infact, a friend of mine moved and had some weed that STRONGLY resembled white widow in EVERY manner growing in the backyard of his new place - and that place hadn't been inhabited for quite a few months, so obviously it does okay outside - but that would also depend on where you live. The move in to whitewidow property was a spot in southern Missouri.

As to what you should do for prepping of the lowrider - it's a fairly hardy strain, so little more than just changing the makeup of the dirt to that of a more nutrient rich storebought or homemmade type. Watering is obvious, but don't plant too near the river - the water level underground might be higher than what the river sits at, so you might accidentily flood your plants if you plant too closeley. Aside from that, occasional fertilization wouldn't hurt, but if it's near a river nutrients are probably all in the soil, and will get absorbed fairly well if your plant's roots leave what you prepared for it, which is most likely. Again, don't plant too near the river.. you never know when some stoner boyscouts might happen your way in a canoe, or worse, an off duty cop in his motorboat.

Re: The OFFICIAL cannabis growing thread
I got bored and wrote this. Please point out any mistakes.

What you will need:

Seeds

Pill bottle or container for seeds

Silica packet (optional)

Paper towel

Bottled drinking water

Tupperware sandwich container (or something like it)

Dixi, or Syrofoam cup

Pencil

Tweezers

Black Plastic or Mulch (optional)

Magnifying glass (Optional)

Glass jars

Paper grocery bags

Gardening equipment (shovel, hoe, ect)

The first step to growing marijuana is of course, seeds. Were can you get seeds? Loads of places. Im going to assume youre growing for the first, I would recommend using what is called bagseed, or the seeds you might find in bag of low quality bud. (If youre lucky, you will find a seed in some top grade product). Start collecting seeds a month or two before you want to start growing. You can keep seeds for years if you store them properly. The ideal conditions for storing seeds are in a dry, cool environment. I personally store mine in a pill bottle with a silica gel packet (the little bag you might find in a bag for beef jerky or something), which absorbs the moisture. If you are confident, or have a bit of extra money to spend, you can buy marijuana seeds online. These are usually of higher quality, and this way you know what strains your getting and you can choose the strain ideal for your growing environment.

The next step is finding a suitable location to grow. This should be away from any paths, nature trails, or houses. Try to find a small clearing, and remember that your plants are going to need direct sunlight. Ideally, there might be a pond, or stream nearby so you dont have to carry water in. Clear all roots and shrubs in about a 4x4 foot area, and use a shovel to turn the dirt over and loosen everything up. If you have money to spend, you can invest in a sack of foxfarm nutrient soil, and mixing that in with the soil thats there. You can buy this at most gardening stores.

Now you have your plot ready, and your seeds, its time for germination. Get your seeds, and dump them into a cup of warm water. Swish it around for a bit. Take all the floaters, and set them on a piece of paper towel. Take the ones that sunk, and toss them. Take 2 sheets of paper towel, and fold them up in half, then in half the other way. Pour your distilled/pure water over them, and squeeze the excess water out. The towel should be damp, but not dripping. Lay these sheets in the bottom of a Tupperware sandwich container. Get one more sheet of paper towel and fold it up the same. Pour water over it, and then squeeze it out just like before. Lay your seeds on the bottom two layers of paper towel, and put the third payer on top of the seeds. Put the lid on the container, and put it somewhere warm. On top of a hot water tank, or if you have an old computer monitor you can put it on there and leave the monitor on all the time. Leave it for 24 hours. Get a Dixi cup, or Styrofoam coffee cup and fill it with soil. Poke a few holes in the bottom, and run some water through it so the soils quite damp (if you bought foxfarm or other soil, use some of that). Take the lid off your Tupperware container, and gently lift up the top layer of paper towel. If you see any seeds that have sprouted, get your cup filled with your damp soil, and use the sharp end of a pencil to make a hole about 2cms deep. Get your tweezers and CAREFULLY, without touching or breaking the little sprout set the seedling in the soil SPROUT DOWN. Flick soil over the hole so its covered, but dont pack it down. Place these cups in a warm sunny place (preferable at your grow location) and keep an eye on them, making sure they are kept damp.

When the seedlings are about 2-3cms out of the soil, its time to plant them in the earth. Squeeze around the sides of the cup so the soil gets loose and you can tip out the entire thing. Dig a hole about the size of the cup, and plop it in. smooth down the soil around it, and water all around the seedling. Keep an eye on your baby/babies and make sure they never dry out. Weed around the marijuana plant so it doesnt have to fight other grass or weeds for survival. When the plant is around 6 inches tall, you can mulch around it with tree leaves (coniferous only, no needles), grass cuttings, or you can get some black plastic from a garbage bag or something and spread it out around your plant in a circle to keep the moisture in, and the unwanted weeds down. Mulching or using black plastic is great, because you dont have to weed, and you dont have to water nearly as much. Just put a few fingers through the mulch/under the plastic and make sure it stays damp.

From this point until harvest, you dont HAVE to do anything. To keep nasty bugs off, grind up some garlic and soak in water. Then spray this on your plant. Usually I dont bother sexing, I just let nature do its job. If you are desperate for more buds, search google.com or something for Marijuana Sexing and pull up the males.

In North America, harvest time is usually around later August, or early September assuming you planted on 4/20 (April 20th). The best way to check if your ready to harvest is to get a high powered magnifying glass, and looking at the buds. If the trichomes (little crystals on the buds) are a milky, cloudy colour your ready.

Now to dry and cure your bud. First, pull the plant up roots and hang it upside down for 24 hours. Then put each plant in a paper grocery bag with the top open for few days or until the leaves feel dry. Take the big leaves off, and put them in a container with a lid. They can be used for hash oil, or cannabutter later. Take whats left, and trim the leaves from the buds with some nail scissors. Put the leaves you trimmed off into a separate jar or container. Now, get as many canning/jam jars as you need and put the trimmed buds in, and close the lid. Every day for a few weeks open it up and shape the buds around. Be careful not to pack the leaves in tightly, you want air to reach all the leaves to prevent mold.

The longer you let the buds cure, they batter theyll be to smoke.

*Rem

Re: The OFFICIAL cannabis growing thread
You want cool whites if you're providing light for a vegging plant. Warm if you want to gain buds.

HPS lights come in the low, 70-125-150 watt ranges around schools, as security lights or anywhere else you can imagine.

Metal Halides, as opposed to the previous high pressure sodium lighting, is much more whiter, as it is lower on the kelvin scale, it is cooler, and are in the same places, usually as parking lot lights, and they provide white looking light, instead of an orange glowing light you'll see around industrial or commercial places. You can find both through.

If you want, pick up an HPS for 109 on Ebay, a 400w, which is useful if you're growing more than a couple large plants.

If you're only creating a small grow room, then your plants will suffice with fluorescent fixtures (4-foot/walmart) with cool temp bulbs, for vegging the seedlings or clones, and then flowering under many warm CFLS, you'd probably do well with picking up a bunch of CFLS some warm and some cold and flowering and vegging throughout with all the light you can get.

Although warm light promotes stem growth and a spreading and thinning out will occur increasing the internodal length between bud sites. While cool light promotes leaf growth and will allow/cause your plant to become bushy and short.

You'll need some sort of fan blowing across the leaves to put a little sway on the plants which will strengthen the stems and allow for meatier buds. Good 3-5 gallon square pots should be used to save space, with holes drilled in the bottoms and sides.

You can LST, to create an even level layer of bud sites, so that there will be less upward growth allowing the buds to get an even amount of light, with not so much lighting. This is using ties or bent stakes to tie the plant down, so that it grows horizontally, while the buds grow vertically around in a spiral in the pot.

The soil should be a higher quality, you don't want to sticks and clumps in the growing medium, and you'll want to pick up enough perlite (the little white balls that retain water and allow root growth+oxygen to pass) to make an at least 30% mix of soil to perlite.

You'll also want to get a soil enhancer like blood or bone meal, or worm or bat casting to mix in the soil for the plants, just don't mix too much, you'll lower your yield.

Vegging and blooming ferts can be found online or in any home and garden store, and should be utilized.

You can pretty much go from there and grow nice bud, there's still more to it though, but that's always dependent on your particular grow room/situation.

haha you don't have to take my advice if you don't want to I'm just saying from my experiences a cabinet grow is a lot more efficient with compact fluorescents. I'm not talking about house bulbs I'm talking about horticultural envirolites.

quote:

Light from the sun is ideal but it's not the same as artificial light, where output quality, spectrum etc varies upon the type of lamp and how it is used. Many growers think that more lumens = better growth / yields, when in fact artificial light, even at its best in a HID or HPS lamp in not so good in terms of colours. Much of the light from the bulb is not used by the plant, mainly because it is not in the 400 to 700 nw (nanawave) spectrum, and plants can only see and use light in this range. Light quality and its colours are as important as lumens.

Light, as seen by plants is not a single colour but separate bands of active colours and the plant senses each colour-band of light as a separate signal. Each band of colour has a different effect on plants and the following are only a few of the functions which each band of light promotes.

Blue Light (350  500 NW) powers chlorophyll production, powers cell actively, energies the stomata movement and makes the plant follow light.

Green / Yellow Light (500  650 nw) ~ not much action from these bands of light.

Red Light (600  700 NW) makes sugar from CO2, powers chloroplast production, signals light and dark times among other functions.

Strong blue and red light photons (as above) are also needed for good carbon dioxide uptake.

The PAR scale measures all these coloured photons between 400nw & 700nw, the critical range for plants, as this is only range that plants can use light. If it is not in this range then it's wasted light.



envirolite cfls are 100% PAR

Also some lights most of you might not have heard of are the spectrum reflex lamps (http://www.spectrumreflex.co.uk)

quote:The Spectrum Reflex lamp was not developed as an energy saving light.

It has been demonstrated that a crop covering one square metre uses, or rather, consumes 150 Watts of electricity during the entire cultivation process. Why then do people use 600/400 Watt bulbs? If you ask experienced growers, the answer youll receive is: light equals yield. So true! But the question is: how much light and what sort of light?



The use of 600/400 Watt bulbs for cultivation has crept in as an established notion. Developing and researching better alternatives has always been difficult.

With these considerations in mind Spectrum Reflex has started a research and development programme that aims to develop more advanced cultivation methods. Its main aim in this was:

- a drastic reduction in power consumption but retaining potential yields that are at least the equivalent of those achieved with conventional methods

Experience has shown that the same yields are possible as those achieved when using sodium lamps, better, in fact, when considering the more favourable light spectrum of the bulb.

quote:Originally posted by panjojo:

Hi, im a first time grower, just finished my outdoor grow box and I have some questions.

My space is about 5 feet by 3 wide, and roughly 4 feet high. I was wondering how many plants I could expect from a room space this size. Im using 2 cool, 2 warm floro 40 watt tubes.

Also, im worried about the smell later on in the grow cycle, is there anything I can do to reduce the smell?

And lastly, my little room is just about sealed. I have a fan in there, but im worried about light polution. Are there any cheap/easy methods for ventelation? (if I need any at all).

Thanks in advance

3x5x4ft could house seven - ten nice plants but you'll need more light, a lot more light.

And you'll need ventilation, plants need to breathe.

You could use a passive air intake which could be a louvred vent in the bottom of your box and have an outtake fan at the top with a carbon filter on if you want to cut down on aroma. You want a fan which will exchange the air inside(sixty cubic feet of it) with freash air completely every 3-5 minutes.

Because of the small size you could use a shower fan(100mm shower fan should have air movement rate of about 85 cubic metres/hour which should more than suffice) or two for the ventilation.

For light you'll want at least 400w of HPS or Envirolites, if you don't want to spend the money just see if you can get more of the fluoro's, get shitloads of 20w cfl housebulbs and their fittings and hang them inside the box.

sooner harvest, with a shorter plant. I later changed it to 18/6 to give them more light. I hope that didnt shock them all to being males. I may have to go up to 24/7 if they dont start to grow some life. What do you guys think? I can get some ferts if need be. Should I transplant?

They're stressed, you shouldn't have added the rose fertiliser, they need no ferts for their first three weeks. Lights at 12/12 from seed is not a good idea, you want to synthesise a good environment for them which works on the same principles as natural outdoor growing.

The 12/12 will have stunted them and they will take some time to build up all the sugars they should have been making in the 12 hours which were dark.

If you can see lots of healthy roots in the bottom of the pots then they're just about ready for transplanting.

You could make up a special dose for the plants by soaking willow bark(salicylic acid boosts the plants immune system and response to stress) in water for a few days then straining the bark out and give a little to them once a week. Wait until they look like they need food before fertilising them and if you're not using ferts specifically designed for cannabis then use 1/4 recommended strength of a balanced NPK(8-8-8 or 10-10-10) with added micronutrients.

Re: The OFFICIAL cannabis growing thread
Sounds good, I take it you're growing mainly sativa's if you want them to grow like indicas?

Although I have never tried putting seedlings under 12/12 straight off, I have been growing for a long time and it just sounds stupid to me. Do you have a reference to where this advice is given, I'd like to see what they're talking about.

With some strains it is possible to put cuttings into 12/12 straight off but not seedlings.

Cannabis plants need a cycle of vegetative growth and unrestricted veg is the key to a healthy harvest. This is especially true for mostly Sativa plants which like long vegetative days. Nine weeks for a grow is sick, you should allocate at least three months for an 8 week flowering plant from seedling, one month veg and two months flowering.

I know you have experience on an organic farm so it shouldn't be too much of a problem, there's just so many different methods people "come up with" for growing cannabis when it's a plant like most others(although it is dioecious) and grows fairly easily if you don't try fancy shit, concerning LST my advice would be for growers and wannabe growers to learn how to cycle before trying to jump. Once you've got a good grow cycle under your belt then try out new things but if you're new to growing just stick to taking care of your plant and letting it show you how it grows.

first page of the RUST thread. about finding sativa mothers by growing from 12/12 seed to identify which ones you plan to keep. IMHO the best use of the 12/12 method.

the reason I didn't make a 12/12 from seed thread is its not a method of growing I reccomend doing. after much experience. I'll bet more than yours.

"so the trick is maximizing space, plant potential, and time. its about finding a mother remember that.

and my answer is 2ltr bottles. veg your sats in 2ltr containers planted densly and flower after just a few weeks. the point is not to get great bud off of it, or yield. the point is to identify your mother ASAP. good plants will be good plants and shit plants will be shit plants from seed. once you find the one that is like you want you can keep it. take the main growth tip for a clone, and once the new tips are taking off happily its okay to flower. this is the long, but safe way to choose a mom.

the idea is rather then spend the time and more importantly an entire light on a strain you know is going to take a long time, you limit it to a few feet of one light, and about 90 some odd days.

the short way is more dangerous but it fits the bill anyway because alot of you don't have veg space to be taking all these clones and waiting to see which ones are good or not. The only real difference is that you only wait 3 days for seedlings to harden up before you flower. don't keep the light that close at first, until they want you too. a cycle should finish anywhere between 75-120 days total from seed. plants will identify themselves sexually after only two weeks. when you select the one you like if you didn't have space to clone then you can reveg. but revegs don't always work. but luckily sativas are predispositioned to reflower/reveg. anyway you want to identify the plant you want. and weed out the rest w/o wasting the time and light on it.

no sense having a light full of one nice plant and six that you'll have to find someone to sell it to.

when you get the one you want THEN you can spend some time and a light on it.

people say the genes change when you reveg but at least IMHO that rarely is the case. I've never noticed much difference. but if you have the option cloning prior to flower is always best for safety if nothing else.

Now remember plants and taste will change with time anyway, but in my experience I've never seen a plant that was superior to the rest be overtaken in quality by a different plant, due to a reveg. The one that was the best before reveg was always the one that was best after reveg.

this is also a good way to grow homemade f2's and 3s."

I guess if you find a plant that suits the regime then it could be very beneficial, I don't have problems with space so I'm not gonna try it but if people are using 12/12 from seed and getting results that's fucking great. I still wouldn't recommend it to anyone on their first few grows.

CO2 in indoor grows makes a lot of difference, I've found that if I were to take a cutting of say a Grapefruit and root it for three days under 24/0 then put it straight into 12/12 with C02 it grows about twice as fast as without and the yields increase beautifully. Bear in mind that this is with 80kg bottles of CO2 on timed release to make it efficient. An constant source of fresh CO2 is one of the kindest things you can do for your plant and they reward you for it.

I can't tell you how much you can expect to yield because I'd be lying, you could get a few grams or you could get two to three ounces, only someone experienced with a plant and who is used to its characteristics could attempt to deduce just how much their chosen plant will yield.

Procedures for excess plant trimmings are down to personal preference, I quite like to save up big bags of it for making bubble hash. I've made oil in the past using the butane method which produces very nice stuff but I like something more containable.

Isn't the vermiculite for the soil mix?


4 Average sized plants would be anything from a 1 to 5 gallon bucket.

5 gallon buckets or around a 12 inch pot can be filled two times over with one of the large sized bags of soil from home depot or something.

You'll mix that with the organics and fillers like vermiculite, blood/bone meal, casting etc etc.

If you get something to mix with soil you can stretch it out, you may only need 1 bag of soil costing anywhere, depending on quality, from 3-10 dollars, or you could need around 3 if you are using large pots.

Depending on how you're going to grow those 10 smaller plants, you would probably only need 1 bag to fill all the smaller pots. For a SOG or something, you won't need anything more than 1-2 gallon pots, that is if you're doing a SOG.

Some inetresting things happened today.
Yesterday I started a south african durban poison x skunk #1 by nicking and soaking it around 6PM.
I microwaved the water to sterilize it, let it cool, then microwaved it a bit to bring it up over 80F.
Then I used a razor blade to scrape the bottom of the seed.
Then I put the seed in the glass and pushed it down a bit with a straw and covered it with aluminum foil.
I kept it ontop of an old TV to keep it warm.
The next day around 12(I think) I took it outside and kept it in direct sunlight.
Later I decided to add another seed.
Around 4 I noticed that the seed had cracked so I gently took it out and put it in a peat pellet.
I noticed it had a little shoot.
It's sitting on top of my monitor right now.

From twelve to around 6PM I spent my time preparing for my grow.
First I took some bannana tree stems and looped some vines through it so it was kind of like a ladder.
Then I climbed my tree next to the spot I was gonna use.
It's hard to describe how the spot is, but there was the trunk then three stem things growing in a triangle close to one another, so it made a nice little crevace for my plant.
There were 2 spots where you could've seen my bag, about 2 x 2 feet kind of triangular(inverted).
Anyways, I took the thing I made and laid it accross one of the spots so it's block my bag from view.
Then I took a kind of thin large black garbage bag and put it inside a tougher one aroung the same size.
I used some thing wire to loop the together near the top.
Put it through 5 spots.
Then I cracked some bricks and stones and gathered small stones to put at the bottom for drainage.
I also used some marbles.
After that I put about 50 quarts of miracle grow moisture control in there, along with some composted chicken & dove poo, decayed leaves, some soil from my garden, and perlite.
It was pretty damn fluffy, so the plant shouldn't have a problem growing some strong roots.
Then I tied some pieces of rope around it so the bag would keep the correct shape.
It was damn hard, had to try a couple of times.
I tied the top of the bag closed so the soil wouldn't spill out when I moved it.
I used one of those things for moving heavy things to bring the bag near the tree.
There's a chain link fence on some horizontal planks right next to the tree that you have to clinb to get on it.
I brought a fold up chair, positioned it on the tree and fence so it was stable, and hoisted the bag on to it.
Then I brought a large ladder and positioned it on the base of the tree where the main parts stem out, so I could carry the bag to the spot.
It was incredibly difficult.
I won't do into details because this is long enough, but believe me, getting it there was MFin'g HARD AS HELL!!!
I put some vines under the rope around the bag and between some stems to hide it.
Got down, cleaned up, and checked my bag(can't see it from any direction).
Tommorow I'm gonna clear away some of the leaves so my plant can get lots of sun.

I wonder if anyone read this monstrocity...
Well, it's pretty satisfying.

Anyways, tommorow I'm gonna go to Home Depot To get some more soil, vermiculite, manure, and fertilizer for the 3 Hindu Kush plants I'm gonna grow.
Anything else I should get?
Are there any fertilizers at home depot that are good for vegetative growth?
Answer fast, if possible, it's late over here.

I am going to share an interesting passive hydro system for outdoor grow ops. Using a two or three liter soda bottle you cut a hole in the lid. Fill it with what ever nutrients you are going to use. Run some wick through the cap, and all the way to the bottom of the bottle with about 6 inches poking out of the top. Dig a hold deep enough to hold the bottle under where you are going to plant and put the wick where the roots would be. Water and nutrients will slowly wick upwards as the plant grows. If you really want to, you could add a fill tube w/ a dipstick to keep the water level full.

No chemicals go on the weed, you water your plants with nothing but pure clean water for the last two weeks before harvest, in order to make sure the root system and veins get cleaned out.

The fertilizer is what you put in the water, slowly, and only with the right amount for your plant, and only when she is ready. You don't want to smoke plant, who hasn't been "flushed" with clean water for a while, otherwise the ferts will be in the product. Which is bad.

ya there stretching. Get them in bigger pots right now, bigger the better. (always better to transfer when small when teres limited roots) Use some anti shock fertilizer when you do it. THen get them outside asap, aslong as your winter is over. THey need the powerfull sun on them and they'll start producing leaves. Also it look like you just used some dirt out of your garden. It would be better to use some store baught soil. THat or just mix some perlite in some garden soil. You can get a bag for a couple bucks. That will give you proper drainage, and nutrient uptake. Most indica weed plants (what people most likely end up with) will absolutly suck the living shit out of the nutrients in the soil. They are very heavy eating plants. So the more nutrients you can give it the bigger and better it will grow. Perlite will help that, aslong as your giving it some nutrients aswell. There thirsty fuckers.

If part of your plant was apale cream color it isn't iron deficiancy it is a nitrogen deficiancy. The nutes you gave her will still help with the nitrogen though. For example during budding you supposed to cut back the nitrogen little by little then at the end of the season they should be getting no nitrogen. As you decrease the nitrogen you shoud be increasing the potassium and phosphorus until they are only getting potassium and phosphorus.

During the light hours, the plant absorbs all the light energy it can, whilst building itself. During the dark hours it uses all the resources it's gathered to grow at a faster rate than it would during the day. As young plants need alot of light, I recommend 24/0 until the 4th set of leaves have developed, then 18/6 till flowering. That is just personal preference though, different strokes for different folks:D

I have heard a plant grown under 24/0 tends to flower slightly earlier, and can be larger, whereas an 18/6 will have a denser concentration of buds.

A 60W fluorescent really isn't enough light, it will provide one plant adequately, but that is about it, don't expect amazing yields either. I really would suggest getting another similar fixture if you insist on fluorescent lighting this grow. 120W fluro will comfortably hold 2 plants and maybe 3 at a stretch.

Due to your restrictive space and light, perhaps you should consider obtaining some clones? It will prevent wasted resources on male vegeing.

Fertilizers aren't really necessary in the first couple of weeks of growth (unless you used really shit soil) and using them over zealously could harm the young plant.

Your soil ideally should have a pH of around 5.5-6.5, oh so slightly basic. Supposedly, acidic soil promotes males, although I don't really see how that is possible considering the sex is predetermined in the seed.

Good luck with your grow. Remember to buy another light!!

Re: The OFFICIAL cannabis growing thread
if one turns out to be male I know you should get rid of any buds to keep the pollen away from females



You should get rid of the males for their pollen, not their buds...

is it worth it to let the plant grown and then save the leaves?


It depends. If you mean leave the male outdoors, away from your females and then harvest it to make hash out of, then sure, go for it. If you mean keep it in the closet, I wouldn't, it reduces the amount of thc in the females because they use alot of their energy to make seeds instead of trics.

and I've read some stuff about growing and some say to let the female grow, induce flowering, and then harvest when about 75% of the pistils change color, but some say that you can cut the female buds and another one will grow in it's place.


You harvest the same time either way, the only difference is that with the latter you don't take the whole stem off you just take the nugs off of it and let more buds grow in it's place. I'm not sure if this works very well, though. It still takes like 2 months for the new buds to grow and your supposed to get a lower yield doing this instead of just cloning or starting a new seed.

so you could get alot more weed out of one plant?
Yes.

what is the norm for this?
It varies, but it's always less than the original harvest.

and if you do pick the buds to let more grow, do you pick them while the pistils are still white or after they change?

You'd be better off picking them when they change (potency wise), but I guess you COULD harvest them at either point in time.

and lastly, is it alright to have the light on 24 hours a day?
It's okay, but most people do 18 hours on 6 hours off for vegging. And you do still have to change to 12 hours of light and 12 hours of dark for flowering (when the buds form).

thanks
You're welcome.

Volcanbaru

Re: The OFFICIAL cannabis growing thread
Would heat be a big problem in a 10' x 12' x 10' room with a 400 watt HPS and little ventilation (moving air from house heating/cooling but no special fan)?

Kinda, but you do NEED to get air moving in the room or your plants will just become shitty(I don't know why, but it happens before). Just get any kind of fan, get regular size one on the plants and big one in the back away from the plants.

Oh and crack a window open a little every once a while for fresh air(Don't forget to cover it up for light escape!)

Re: The OFFICIAL cannabis growing thread
Hmm, for some reason I was getting worried that I was letting my lowryder 2s mature too long. Turns out they sprouted around the beggining of may, so they still have until between the end of the month and the 15th. It's a pretty interesting plant. Really taught me the basics and allowed me to do some hands on work. Right now I have one supper stubby plant that's a freaking stout bush, it was impossible to low stress train properly. Another one responded to low stress training very nicely. One that I planted later is kinda small and disappointing. The last one that's part of the second group I planted is a lot bigger than my other plants, it's very impressive.

My big bud stealth grows are going great. The one on the roof is responding really well to low stress training. It's gonna be a big healthy bush. The other one is in a tree and it's kinda akward due to the shade, so I'm not gonna low stress train it. It's pretty healthy, so I should get a decent yield.

Oi, I still haven't gotten around to pollinating a portion of my lowryders for seeds. If one of my big bud plants is a male(I hope not) I'd like to pollinate the lowryders with its pollen. Hmm, I suppose I could still fit in another grow just for seeds after my lowryders are done. They'd have to survive august through october, but they are autoflowering. They wouldn't have a problem until winter. Damn, I wish there was a place where I could buy pollen. There's no way in hell you'd get caught sending it in an envelope.
